feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior digital communications CV with clear positioning, credible scope, and relevant public-sector leadership experience. It reads professionally and shows progression well, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong progression at NACo into director-level ownership of web, analytics, governance, and multimedia.  
- Good credibility through scale indicators: 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers, and named tools/platforms.  
- Broad but coherent skill set spanning strategy, CMS/platform delivery, analytics, and content operations.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve structure and scannability.  
- Add more outcome-focused impact: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results. Include measurable improvements in engagement, efficiency, adoption, cost savings, or campaign performance.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “organization-wide”/“member-facing” hyphenation is good but should stay consistent throughout; “A2/Learning” is awkward—use “A2 (learning)”; “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is stylistically inconsistent unless intentional branding.  

No major misspellings found. Writing quality is strong overall, but tightening repetition and standardizing style would make it more polished.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible positioning with clear seniority and public-sector relevance. However, it overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and recent experience, and would be stronger with one or two concrete signals of scale.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and make more distinctive: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years shaping the platforms, governance, and content operations behind large-scale public-sector communications.”
- Add scale from recent roles to increase impact, e.g., “Led enterprise web modernization for a 10,000+ page Drupal platform serving 3.5M annual page views and 50+ publishers.”
- Replace the generic second sentence with sharper scope: “Combines digital strategy, analytics, editorial systems, multimedia production, and AI-enabled search to improve how mission-driven organizations publish, measure, and serve users.”
- Use parallel style and consistent phrasing: “platforms, governance, and content operations” rather than a longer mixed list.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” repeats ideas already covered in Core Competencies and Recent Projects.
- The subtitle already signals leadership; avoid restating “Senior digital leader” if space is tight.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be more effective if tightened, made more parallel in style, and focused on highest-value differentiators rather than broad category labels.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, more scannable noun phrases with consistent structure; avoid mixing “operations,” “systems,” and “communications” unevenly.
- Prioritize distinctive strengths tied to recent work: enterprise web modernization, governance, analytics, AI search, automation/integration, and public-sector digital communications.
- Consider trimming to 6–7 items to increase impact and reduce repetition.
- Possible rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards, and reporting infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization” and “AI-enabled search and content experiences” repeat language already used in the header.
- Several items substantially overlap with the more detailed Topline Skills section, especially analytics, multimedia, and workflow automation.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and overlaps with work-experience bullets. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing outcomes, scope, or distinct formats will make it feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a short intro line like “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use consistent action/result structure: “Built/Developed [project] featuring [key elements] to [purpose/outcome].”
- Tighten wording: change “designed for continued campaign growth” to “built for future campaign expansion”; spell out “10-by-20-foot” for style consistency.
- Consider this rewrite: “Selected recent projects: AI Hybrid Search—Built an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search, and bill-level chat to improve policy discovery. We Are Counties Microsite—Developed a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling, downloadable resources, and reusable modules for future expansion. Organization Anniversary Campaign—Created a multi-part digital campaign blending editorial storytelling, archival media, web features, and a 10-by-20-foot interactive conference display. Advocacy Video Series—Launched a recurring advocacy video series spanning planning, production, and distribution across web, email, and social.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search and Advocacy Video Series closely repeat achievements already covered in recent roles.
- Drupal microsite language overlaps with the current freelance role; keep this block more portfolio-style than responsibility-based.

### Recent Projects

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, skills, and project section. Tighten it around outcomes, scale, and the most senior-value work: platform modernization, governance, and AI search.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise”) with ownership language: led, built, redesigned, launched, standardized, improved.
- Consolidate into 4–5 bullets focused on impact, e.g. Drupal campaign builds, org-wide workflows/analytics, governance across channels, and AI-enabled search.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages, users, publishers, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search accuracy, time saved, publishing speed, or engagement gains.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search initiative” duplicates the Recent Projects section; keep this bullet higher-level here and let the project section hold the technical detail.
- “Governance, usability, and operational best practices” overlaps with prior NACo roles; specify what changed or improved in this engagement.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. Tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management points covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web modernization, multi-channel communications, analytics, governance, and budget oversight.”
- Lead with the flagship achievement: “Spearheaded redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more outcome-focused: add email/social growth, engagement, or campaign performance metrics if available; otherwise shorten to one line.
- Strengthen impact wording: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing internal production capacity for advocacy, events, and recurring multimedia content” and “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting to improve decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this version strategic, not operational.
- Video-program language may duplicate older NACo roles unless framed here as studio-building and scale.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads generic and overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Tighten it around scope, ownership, and channel growth/operational impact.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper lead: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial operations and advocacy messaging for a national public-sector audience.”
- Replace “helping” language with direct ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters…,” “Launched/grew a weekly advocacy video update…,” “Built cross-team editorial planning…”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: newsletter audience size/open rates, video cadence/views, turnaround time, publishing volume, or number of teams/stakeholders coordinated.
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger operations bullet: “Built more consistent editorial calendars and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and content delivery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly advocacy video update” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and the footer project; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the series.
- “Digital communications across web, email, social and video” overlaps with the 2022–2024 Director role; keep this one focused on execution and workflow leadership, not enterprise oversight.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership

items.title: University of Virginia

Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/recent CMS platforms or add light context on level of use.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize most relevant platforms first: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages**; move **GitHub Pages** to Coding/Technical Implementation or remove if not central.
- If space allows, add proficiency framing: **Enterprise CMS: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages**.
- Consider a more impact-linked label: **CMS & Web Platforms** instead of **Web Platforms & CMS**.
- If you want stronger differentiation, use tiers: **Primary: Drupal, WordPress | Supporting: SharePoint, Power Pages**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates Topline Skills [2], which already lists the same platforms plus broader technical capabilities.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles; avoid repeating the same platform list in multiple sections without added context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools you actively use in recent roles and group items more strategically.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Add a second grouped phrase: “Technical delivery: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- If accurate, strengthen with scope/context rather than versions: replace “HTML5 • CSS3” with “semantic HTML, responsive CSS” for a more senior tone
- Consider renaming the heading to “Front-End & Technical Delivery” to better match the content and avoid sounding entry-level

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; keep the fuller version in one place only
- “Workflow automation” in Topline Skills may overlap with GitHub Actions; decide whether automation lives here or under Automation & Workflow Systems

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. Since “workflow automation” and Airtable systems already appear elsewhere, this item should be tighter and more category-led to avoid repetition.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from a flat list to grouped systems: “Workflow automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/issue management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Team collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams.”
- Put the strongest, most relevant tools first: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana.
- If space allows, add a light qualifier tied to impact: “used to support cross-team planning, approvals, and communications workflows.”
- Consider dropping one or two lower-value/general tools if they were not central to recent work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack and Teams are common collaboration tools; keep them only if they were meaningfully used in operational systems leadership.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too bare to add much value. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this line should emphasize platform depth and avoid restating channel ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform naming for readability: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope in parentheses to show practical use, e.g. **Higher Logic (member email/newsletters)**, **Dynamics 365 CI-Journeys (campaign automation)**, **Mailchimp (list management/templates)**
- If one platform was primary in the 2022–2024 director role, list it first to reflect recency and strength

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email newsletters and digital channels; keep this item platform-focused, not responsibility-focused
- Avoid adding generic terms like “email campaigns” or “engagement strategy” here, since those are already covered elsewhere

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” In a technical section, tighten it to platforms/methods and make the optimization angle more precise.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: **GA4 • BigQuery • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Search Console • KPI reporting • Experimentation**
- Swap broad terms like **SEO** and **Dashboarding** for more concrete skill labels: **technical SEO / search performance analysis** and **executive dashboarding / KPI reporting**
- If space allows, group by function for readability: **Analytics:** GA4, BigQuery, Clarity | **Reporting:** Looker Studio, Power BI | **Optimization:** technical SEO, experimentation
- Only keep **A/B testing** if you’ve directly run experiments; otherwise **Experimentation** is safer and broader

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider trimming one or making this version tools-only
- “Dashboarding” overlaps with Looker Studio/Power BI, so it reads repetitive unless reframed as **executive KPI reporting**

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational: emphasize team-building, early platform/content execution, and any concrete scale or output.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground progression and first-team build: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Add specific outputs if available: number of livestreams/videos produced, frequency of updates, size/timing of website refresh, channels supported, or team size.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce generic terms like “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows”; replace with actions and outcomes.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations. Contributed to a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and helped formalize day-to-day publishing workflows while informally guiding a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; distinguish this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- “Strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; keep this entry more execution-focused.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the podcast launch and frame research/project coordination more concretely.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county policy and program teams; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, guest coordination, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a clearer scope: “produced multimedia and digital content to support program communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, add 1 measurable detail: number of episodes, stakeholders supported, projects coordinated, or audience/reach.
- Keep this entry shorter than later NACo roles so progression is clear.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating generic multimedia/video language already covered in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overstate digital leadership here; save team/operations scale for the 2018–2024 positions.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
